content.text: {"title":"Cutcraft Trail","summary":"Build story judgment through short editing repetitions, then deliver and explain a complete sixty-second sequence. Each stage moves from intentional cuts to a finished documentary artifact.","world":{"name":"Cutcraft Citadel","tagline":"Every cut must earn the next frame."},"stages":[{"title":"Story Gate","theme":"See before you cut","summary":"Learn to identify the story purpose behind a sequence.","quests":[{"type":"mission","title":"Frame the Story","objective":"Create a six-shot paper edit with a clear beginning, change, and ending.","brief":"Choose six moments from a short source and arrange them before touching transitions.","lesson":{"principle":"Story intention comes before polish","explanation":"A cut is useful when it changes information, emotion, or time for a reason.","example":"Open with context, reveal the central action, and end on the consequence."},"durationMinutes":30,"xp":110,"skills":["Story judgment"],"steps":["Name the one-sentence story.","Select six necessary moments.","Arrange and review without transitions."],"successCriteria":["The sequence has a visible beginning, change, and ending.","Every selected shot has a stated story purpose.","One unnecessary shot was removed after review."],"reflectionPrompt":"Which cut changed the meaning most, and why?"},{"type":"mission","title":"Cut on Meaning","objective":"Build two versions of one moment using different cut points.","brief":"Compare how timing changes what the viewer notices.","lesson":{"principle":"Cut timing directs attention","explanation":"Holding or cutting earlier changes emphasis even when the source is identical.","example":"Cut before a reaction for surprise; hold through it for empathy."},"durationMinutes":30,"xp":120,"skills":["Timing"],"steps":["Choose one reaction moment.","Make an early-cut version.","Make a hold-through version and compare."],"successCriteria":["Two distinct versions exist.","The intended effect of each is written down.","One preferred version is justified."],"reflectionPrompt":"What changed when the cut moved?"},{"type":"side","title":"Audio Before Picture","objective":"Use one audio lead to create continuity between two shots.","brief":"Practise a small J-cut without adding decorative effects.","lesson":{"principle":"Sound can carry the viewer across a visual change","explanation":"An audio lead prepares the next scene before the picture arrives.","example":"Let the next speaker begin just before the visual cut."},"durationMinutes":25,"xp":100,"skills":["Audio continuity"],"steps":["Choose adjacent moments.","Move the next audio earlier.","Review with eyes closed and open."],"successCriteria":["The transition remains understandable.","The audio lead has a stated purpose.","Levels do not distract from the story."],"reflectionPrompt":"Did sound make the cut feel more intentional?"}]},{"title":"Rhythm Forge","theme":"Shape attention","summary":"Practise pacing, continuity, and feedback-driven revision.","quests":[{"type":"mission","title":"Thirty-Second Pulse","objective":"Edit a thirty-second sequence around one emotional beat.","brief":"Use shot duration to make the emotional change legible.","lesson":{"principle":"Rhythm is the pattern of attention","explanation":"Pacing becomes meaningful when duration follows the story rather than a preset tempo.","example":"Longer holds can create weight before a short decisive cut."},"durationMinutes":35,"xp":130,"skills":["Timing","Story judgment"],"steps":["Mark the emotional change.","Build a rough rhythm.","Remove one cut that adds no meaning."],"successCriteria":["The emotional change is identifiable.","Shot duration supports that change.","At least one revision is documented."],"reflectionPrompt":"Where did the sequence breathe or rush?"},{"type":"mission","title":"Continuity Under Pressure","objective":"Repair one continuity problem without hiding the story.","brief":"Diagnose the break, then choose the smallest clear fix.","lesson":{"principle":"Continuity serves comprehension","explanation":"A technically smooth cut still fails when viewers lose spatial or narrative orientation.","example":"Insert a purposeful orientation shot rather than covering every cut with B-roll."},"durationMinutes":35,"xp":140,"skills":["Continuity"],"steps":["Name the continuity break.","Try two possible repairs.","Choose the clearer version."],"successCriteria":["The original problem is identified.","Two repairs were compared.","The final sequence stays understandable."],"reflectionPrompt":"What clue restored orientation?"},{"type":"boss","title":"The Rough-Cut Trial","objective":"Deliver a forty-five-second rough cut and explain five key edit decisions.","brief":"Combine story intention, timing, audio continuity, and revision in one complete rough cut.","lesson":{"principle":"A rough cut tests the whole story system","explanation":"Completeness exposes relationships that isolated drills cannot.","example":"Screen the sequence once for story, once for sound, and once for pacing."},"durationMinutes":70,"xp":240,"skills":["Story judgment","Timing","Continuity"],"steps":["Complete the full rough cut.","Review in three focused passes.","Explain five consequential decisions."],"successCriteria":["A complete forty-five-second sequence exists.","Five edit decisions have stated reasons.","One revision follows a focused review pass."],"reflectionPrompt":"Which system-level weakness appeared only after the sequence was complete?"}]},{"title":"Field Screening","theme":"Make it hold up","summary":"Use critique, explain decisions, and recover from a weak cut.","quests":[{"type":"mission","title":"One-Viewer Test","objective":"Run a structured comprehension test with one viewer or a self-review protocol.","brief":"Collect observations without defending the cut.","lesson":{"principle":"Observation is more useful than approval","explanation":"Feedback improves a cut when it reveals where viewer understanding differs from intent.","example":"Ask what changed in the story rather than whether the edit was good."},"durationMinutes":30,"xp":150,"skills":["Feedback practice"],"steps":["Write two neutral questions.","Observe the response.","Choose one evidence-based revision."],"successCriteria":["Questions do not lead the reviewer.","Observed confusion or clarity is recorded.","One revision follows the evidence."],"reflectionPrompt":"Where did viewer understanding differ from your intent?"},{"type":"mission","title":"Edit Decision Defense","objective":"Explain the purpose of ten cuts in plain language.","brief":"Separate intentional choices from habits and decoration.","lesson":{"principle":"Explanation reveals judgment","explanation":"If a choice cannot be connected to story, attention, emotion, or time, it may be habit.","example":"I cut here to reveal the reaction before the speaker explains it."},"durationMinutes":35,"xp":160,"skills":["Editorial reasoning"],"steps":["Select ten cuts.","Write one reason for each.","Replace one weakly justified cut."],"successCriteria":["Ten decisions have clear reasons.","Reasons connect to viewer experience.","One habitual choice was revised."],"reflectionPrompt":"Which decision was hardest to justify?"},{"type":"side","title":"Broken-Cut Rescue","objective":"Diagnose and repair the weakest five seconds of a sequence.","brief":"Make a precise repair instead of restarting the entire edit.","lesson":{"principle":"Diagnosis beats random tweaking","explanation":"A named problem suggests a testable change.","example":"If orientation is unclear, test the order before changing every transition."},"durationMinutes":30,"xp":150,"skills":["Editorial reasoning","Continuity"],"steps":["Name the weakest moment.","State one cause.","Test one targeted repair."],"successCriteria":["The problem is described precisely.","The repair targets the stated cause.","Before-and-after evidence exists."],"reflectionPrompt":"Did the diagnosis predict the useful repair?"}]},{"title":"Final Projection","theme":"Prove the craft","summary":"Simulate real delivery, polish the strongest evidence, and complete the target sequence.","quests":[{"type":"mission","title":"Deadline Simulation","objective":"Complete a bounded edit under a realistic delivery time.","brief":"Plan the passes before the timer begins and protect story clarity first.","lesson":{"principle":"Constraints reveal priorities","explanation":"A deadline tests whether the editor can protect the most important decisions.","example":"Reserve separate passes for structure, audio, and final checks."},"durationMinutes":60,"xp":180,"skills":["Independent delivery"],"steps":["Plan the review passes.","Complete within the timebox.","Record what was protected or deferred."],"successCriteria":["A complete deliverable exists.","The timebox was respected.","Trade-offs are documented."],"reflectionPrompt":"Which priority survived the deadline, and which did not?"},{"type":"mission","title":"Portfolio Polish","objective":"Refine the strongest sequence and prepare a concise process note.","brief":"Use saved feedback and criteria rather than adding unplanned decoration.","lesson":{"principle":"Polish is evidence-led refinement","explanation":"The final pass should strengthen intent and remove distraction.","example":"Fix the two moments that most affect comprehension before touching cosmetic details."},"durationMinutes":45,"xp":190,"skills":["Feedback practice","Editorial reasoning"],"steps":["Review saved feedback.","Choose two high-impact refinements.","Write the process note."],"successCriteria":["Refinements trace to saved evidence.","The sequence is export-ready.","The process note explains key decisions."],"reflectionPrompt":"Which refinement made the largest difference?"},{"type":"boss","title":"The Sixty-Second Summit","objective":"Deliver and explain a complete sixty-second documentary sequence.","brief":"Combine story, timing, sound, continuity, feedback, and delivery into the final outcome.","lesson":{"principle":"A finished artifact is the clearest learning evidence","explanation":"The final sequence demonstrates how the trained abilities work together.","example":"Present the sequence, the intended viewer experience, and five decisions that shaped it."},"durationMinutes":70,"xp":280,"skills":["Independent delivery","Story judgment","Editorial reasoning"],"steps":["Finish and export the sequence.","Run final story and audio checks.","Explain five decisions and the next improvement."],"successCriteria":["A complete sixty-second documentary sequence exists.","The intended viewer experience is stated.","Five edit decisions and one future improvement are explained."],"reflectionPrompt":"What does this final sequence prove, and what will your next project train?"}]}],"skillTree":[{"name":"Story judgment","description":"Choose moments and cuts for narrative purpose."},{"name":"Timing","description":"Shape viewer attention through cut placement and duration."},{"name":"Audio continuity","description":"Use sound to carry meaning across visual changes."},{"name":"Editorial reasoning","description":"Explain, critique, and revise editing decisions."},{"name":"Independent delivery","description":"Complete a coherent sequence under realistic constraints."}]}
